note: Candidate counterexample from SCG II.80 n.13 (claim AQUINAS-SCG-II-80-UNITED-SOUL-ESSE-RECEIVED-BY-BODY). Take x = a human soul united to the body and r = the body. If that is EsseReceivedIn x r in the sense of DEF-ESSE-RECEIVED-IN (receiving potency to received act), then the premise forces the body to be the soul's essence. Aquinas denies this: the soul is a form whose esse does not depend on matter. So the premise would be false of the united soul. Whether it is a real counterexample depends on the sense of 'recipiens'. (a) Same sense: the body is in potency to the soul's esse as to its act. ST I q.76 a.1 ad 5 (passage AQUINAS-ST-I-Q76-A1, read) says the soul 'illud esse in quo ipsa subsistit, communicat materiae corporali', so corporeal matter does receive the soul's own esse. On this reading the attack holds, and the premise's 'every principle in which x's esse is received' must be restricted, for example to the principle in which x's esse is received as x's own, or to subsistent beings not united to matter. (b) Different sense: the body receives the esse of the composite human being, which the soul shares with it. The same ad 5 continues 'ita quod illud esse quod est totius compositi, est etiam ipsius animae', so one esse is both the composite's and the soul's. Then the receiver is a co-principle of the human essence, and the reception in the soul's own quiddity (De ente c.4) is untouched. On this reading there is no counterexample, but the premise's x must then range over the composite and not the soul, and its equality r = essenceOf x still fails for matter as a mere part of the human essence. (c) Restricted scope: the sentence concerns only the soul 'dum est corpori unita', so a separated soul or a pure intelligence is not attacked. Recorded as an objection, not a refutation: the reading choice is open, and nothing in Lean encodes it. A refutation would need the soul, the body and their esse typed in the EsseReceivedIn vocabulary under reading (a), with the body shown distinct from the soul's essence.
